form.notes: Form-associated (ElementInternals): submits `name=value` (an empty string when nothing is chosen), resets to the `value` attribute, restores on navigation, joins <fieldset disabled>, works with form= and label for. `required` is a constraint (valueMissing, with the browser's own localized message); the error is shown after a change, a submit attempt or `reportValidity()` (aria-invalid, announced once).

differences.text: Uncontrolled by default (D-006): `value` is a string with the `value` attribute as its default, `""` means nothing is chosen (upstream `undefined`), and native `input`/`change` events report a user change instead of a controlled `value` plus `onChange`. Nothing is chosen submits `name=` with an empty string.

The `is*` props are bare boolean attributes (`disabled`, `readonly`, `required`, `optional`, `label-hidden`, `loading`), `htmlName` is `name` and `isDefaultOpen` is the `open` attribute, which is also the live state; `xstyle` and `data-testid` are replaced by class, style, `::part()` and host attributes.
`has-clear` sets the value to `""` (upstream reports `null`/`undefined`) and fires the cancelable `tct-clear` before it clears, from the button and from Delete or Backspace on the closed trigger.

The selection mark of a row and of the multi selector is drawn by the three shipped indicator elements (check, checkbox, radio) chosen through the indicator registry; a theme-replaced indicator tag is not drawn in rows (the templates cannot render an arbitrary tag name without `unsafeStatic`, which the lint bans).

The popup opens below the trigger by default. Placing the chosen row over the trigger (upstream default, `useSelectedItemOffset`) is opt-in with `placement="overlay"`; `above`, `below`, `start` and `end` and `alignment` position it as for every anchored surface.

The state of an async option source is `options-state` (`ready`, `loading`, `error`), independent of `loading` (the busy value). Options you provide stay selectable in every state; an empty panel says which state it is (`loading-text`, `error-text`, `empty-text`) and is announced exactly once when the state arrives (AST-001).

The opening keys (click, Enter, Space, ArrowDown) highlight the chosen option, and the first when nothing is chosen; ArrowUp highlights the chosen option, else the last (WAI-ARIA APG select-only combobox). The highlight is `aria-activedescendant` on the combobox (element reflection, id fallback in Tier 2); DOM focus stays on the trigger or the search field.

With `has-search` the search field inside the popup is the combobox (the trigger drops its role while the list is open) and Home and End move its caret; PageUp and PageDown always jump to the first or last option.

The trigger is the shared Tecton outlined field (or the tertiary action fill for `ghost`); the popup is a 1px rule on the recessed popover fill with no drop shadow (D-013) and rows hover through the Tecton table-row fills.

provisional: The popup's height cap (340px, the upstream 300px list plus the search row) follows upstream; no Tecton design frame was compared.
